Finally, the RL model features a performance-based curriculum learning structure [27], [28], [29], which adjusts the level of task di culty by dynamically modifying the level of acceptable error [21], thereby allowing the RL-AAN controller to not only adjust the assistance level but also to scale task di culty based on user performance.

First, the acceptable error thresholds ( low , med , and high ) were manually set to uniform values across all participants, and the network learning rates ( c , a ) were defined from pilot data. This approach intro- duces subjectivity and may not generalize well to users with heterogeneous functional impairments.

In terms of experimental design, incorporating a control condition with visual feedback but no physical guidance would be valuable for elucidating how RL- and ILC-based assistance compare to unassisted practice.

While this study suggests the e ectiveness of the RL-AAN algorithm in inducing short-term motor adaptations in healthy individuals, additional work is required before this approach can be piloted in individuals post-stroke.
